comments.text: Two inverse screen-code digits copied into the status display; Mystery Maze file variants share number25.
Initial placement-stream pointer consumed by resident $7514/$4D0F before the private initialization callback.
Background and border color bytes. Loader uses pristine backup $3804/$3805 when publishing VIC colors.
Seven-byte bomb record pointer. The scanner searches for key $FF; target count $3013 need not equal record count. PLF13 uniquely omits the terminator after its four intended records.
Four pending callback pointers copied by $758A into $40C8-$40CF. A zero high byte leaves the existing no-op task; nonzero vectors are committed by the resident IRQ.
Initial player X low, X high and Y in hardware sprite coordinates, read by spawn $56E0. This is the start of each life, not multicolor drawing coordinates.
Initial target counter 12. Collection decrements it; special bomb callbacks can compensate the decrement or replace the table. Primary record list has 16 entries.
Resident perimeter-bullet slot limit 2; $6800 considers sprite slots1 through limit-minus-one. Private level actors can use other slots.
Ordinary collection adds this little-endian binary value (100) to the24-bit total score. Private callbacks may add an extra award first.
Initial little-endian bonus 1500. The resident countdown subtracts100 per256 enabled IRQ services; completion adds the remaining amount to total and bonus records.
Private initialization routine called after initial scenery drawing. Common no-op target is the RTS at $301F.
Main-thread entry selected by JMP($301B) at $759C; typically the spawn/collection/exit loop at $3050.
Private cleanup hook copied into the local JSR trampoline before completion or exhaustion. A target of $301F returns immediately.
Shared one-byte RTS used by empty initialization, cleanup and individual bomb callbacks in this overlay.
Eight ladder/up-rope X columns followed by six down-rope X columns, copied to $40B0-$40BD. Coordinates use160-wide multicolor space; $FF marks unavailable columns.
Two zero header bytes between the climb-column arrays and completion vector; the shared loader does not read them as part of those arrays.
Ordinary successful-level destination $5B00. The private loop calls cleanup before jumping through this word.
Exhausted-lives destination $5FFD, the resident jump to game-over presentation $6A80. This is separate from successful completion.
Two filename suffix characters '08'. Resident loader copies them into $40D3/$40D4; private cleanup can replace them before the next disk request.
Single $FF drawing-stream terminator, used as the no-change post-bomb action.
Zero byte after the empty drawing terminator and before collection-key coordinate offsets.
X/Y offsets applied by resident $55BF when reducing player position to the bomb lookup key. They adjust the coarse cell test, not the visible bomb positions.
Optional hook called before the matched bomb-record callback. A zero high byte suppresses the call; otherwise the resident patches JSR $5643 from this word.
Twenty loaded zero bytes align the private main loop to $3050. Header fields end at $303B; no private structure is assigned to this gap.

Spawn/reveal a life through $436A, then repeatedly check bomb collection through $436D. Zero remaining count at $3013 exits through success vector $3030 after setting divisor 9; death state $4028=2 waits for state 0, then respawns unless lives sentinel $40E4=$FF, which exits through $3032. Both exits call the header cleanup pointer.

Patch local JSR operand from little-endian header $301D/$301E, invoke cleanup, return. In this file the header resolves to shared no-op RTS at $301F; the assembled $FFFF target is a placeholder, not a real call.

Fourth callback requestsdeath 1 on nonzero $402B while state 0 only if player collision mask contains any bits 1..5 (mask 3E). Sprites 6/7 used for reward/ladder feedback do not by themselves kill the player.

Drawing data $30AD-$3131 read by Initial scenery $30AD. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.

16 seven-byte records [coarse key,x,y,callback low/high,post-draw low/high]. Terminator: $FF. Coordinates are160-wide bitmap positions. The resident scanner matches the key, calls both hooks, adds $3015 points, erases the bomb, follows the draw pointer and decrements $3013. This list is not bounded by the target counter.

Drawing data $31A3-$31D8 read by Post-bomb drawing $31A3, Post-bomb drawing $31AD, Post-bomb drawing $31B7, Post-bomb drawing $31BE, Post-bomb drawing $31C5, Post-bomb drawing $31CF. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.
Third callback mirrors player X-low, X-high andY into sprite 7 state $406A/$4072/$407A, so the special marker tracks the player exactly.

Second callback requires marker enabled $4062, playerX exactly 176 with X-high 0, and playerY exactly target $3244 (initial 122). Queue $332A, patch redrawY to playerY-50, decrement targetY by 8, draw stream $323D, then disable marker until another eligible bomb callback re-enables it.
Seven-byte drawing stream FE,$7E56, then placementX76,Yself-modified at $3241,count 1,FF. Called by $31EC to advance the central puzzle geometry.
PlayerY threshold initially 122; each successful centred ladder activation subtracts 8. It is compared for exact equality, not a range.
Per-bomb callback for eight ordinary bombs: set sprite 7 enabled-state $4062=1, allowing next centred activation in $31EC.

One meaningful compact 30-byte frame, expanded into slot $10/$8400 by $4376. The loader still reads 240 bytes total and copies following code/data into the seven remaining slots; dedicated $3317 then replaces slot $11.
Expand compact marker $324B, set sprite 7 colour 6, frame 10 and initiallydisabled. Jump $3317 to install the score-award sprite in slot $11.
Per-bomb callback on four top records: add 400 ($0190) to 24-bit total $40DA-DC, in addition to the shared 100-point bomb award. Set popup timer $329E=$79; no direct bonus-total update here.
Countdown 121 callbacks for the special-score popup. Initial timer 79 triggers copying player location to sprite 6; expiration disables the sprite.

First callback disables ladder marker during nonzero deathstate. If popup timerstarts 79, place sprite 6 at player coordinates and enable it; increment its colour each callback, decrement timer, and hide at 0.
63 authored bitmap bytes (one full 24 x 21 VIC sprite) for the special-bomb score popup. $3317 copies 64 bytes: the 64 th is its own first opcodeA2, serving as unused spritepadding only.
Copy 64 bytes from $32D8 to $8440 and set sprite 6 pointer 11. Only first 63 copiedbytes are visible pixels; finalbyte is opcodeA2 from this routine, illustrating an ignored spritepadding overread.
Sound envelope 00/40 then six identical frequency 1010 notes of 4 ticks, followed 0. Queued as priority 6, release 2, noise 80 on each successful ladder step.

Unreachable retained variant of PLF06 shooting/falling/collision code, with shifted private-variable addresses. This file vectors target only $308F/$31D9/$31EC/$329F; no private call reaches the residue. Whole $3340-$37FF equals PLF08 at corresponding addresses.
Loaded FF/00/80/7F pattern residue after the stale shooting fragment, byte-identical to PLF08; no active sprite source or pointer reaches here.
